student_learning_goal: I can show that fractions like 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8, 1/3 = 2/6, and 1/5 = 2/10 are equivalent using fraction strips and drawings.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can show that fractions like 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8, 1/3 = 2/6, and 1/5 = 2/10 are equivalent using fraction strips and drawings.
header.character_watermark: Frankie, Penny, and Sammy together in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall combined).

image_placeholders.description: Three equivalence chains in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each ~7in × 0.8in. Chain 1: 1/2 = ___/4 = ___/8. Chain 2: 1/3 = ___/6. Chain 3: 1/5 = ___/10.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; three chains.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P1_THREE_CHAINS: keywords (equivalence, fractions) name what the chains ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Three same-size pizzas. Shade matching equivalent fractions. Write the equation.
parts.visual_layout: Middle. Three pizzas side by side.

image_placeholders.description: Three same-size circular pizzas in B&W line-art, side by side. Each ~2.5in diameter. Pizza A divided into 2 halves. Pizza B divided into 4 fourths. Pizza C divided into 8 eighths. Below: 'Shade 1/2 of A, 2/4 of B, 4/8 of C. Equation: ___/2 = ___/4 = ___/8.'
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; three pizzas in a row.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P2_THREE_PIZZAS: keywords (pizza, equivalent) name what the pizzas show.

parts.answer_key: Pizza A: shade 1 of 2 sectors. Pizza B: shade 2 of 4 sectors. Pizza C: shade 4 of 8 sectors. Equation: 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8.

parts.student_instructions: For each claim, circle TRUE or FALSE. Write 1 line of reasoning.

image_placeholders.description: Six equivalence-claim rows in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each ~7in × 0.5in. Format: claim on left (e.g., '1/2 = 4/8'), TRUE/FALSE bubbles, reason line. Claims: 1/2 = 4/8, 1/3 = 2/4, 1/4 = 2/8, 1/2 = 2/3, 1/5 = 3/15, 2/4 = 4/6.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P3_SIX_CLAIMS: keywords (true, false) name what the rows ask for.

parts.answer_key: 1/2 = 4/8 TRUE (×4 both). 1/3 = 2/4 FALSE (would need to multiply by same factor). 1/4 = 2/8 TRUE (×2 both). 1/2 = 2/3 FALSE (different multipliers). 1/5 = 3/15 TRUE (×3 both). 2/4 = 4/6 FALSE (different multipliers; 2/4 = 1/2 = 4/8, NOT 4/6).

parts.student_instructions: Why does 1/2 equal 2/4? Draw a picture and write 1-2 sentences.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank box with drawing area and writing lines.

image_placeholders.description: A blank rectangular box in B&W line-art, ~7in × 2.5in, with light-grey solid outline. Top half is drawing area; bottom half is 3 lined writing rows. Frankie thinking-bubble icon in the top-right.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P4_WHY_BOX: keywords (equivalent) name what the box asks for.

parts.answer_key: Open. Accept any plausible reasoning that touches on (a) the SAME amount of pizza is shaded and (b) more cuts make smaller pieces but more of them. Examples: '1/2 and 2/4 cover the same amount of pizza. The pizza is just cut differently.' 'Multiplying top and bottom by 2 gives an equivalent fraction.'

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, write 3 more equivalence pairs of your own using denominators between 2 and 12.
teacher_notes: Lesson 5 capstone summative worksheet. Use Parts 1-4 as summative evidence for B1.7. Part 4 reasoning is the deepest understanding marker — children who can articulate the SAME-AMOUNT-OF-PIZZA insight are at L4. Watch for Part 3 children who write TRUE for 1/3 = 2/4 (the additive fallacy) — flag for the multiplication-pattern reteach.
